Hull, Coventry and Ipswich have already collected 24 points between them after six games, so the conversation is starting to shift from pre-season vibes on whether all three newly-promoted clubs will be relegated to which established Premier League names could be in the scrap for survival. The Premier League's newly-promoted sides have often struggled to bridge the gap, with two consecutive seasons in 2023/24 and 2024/25 seeing all three newcomers relegated before Leeds and Sunderland helped buck that trend last season. messages.text: Infantino under pressure after second £1.3m salary revealed

metadata.summary: FIFA president Gianni Infantino is under increasing pressure to resign after it was revealed that he received an undeclared second salary of £1.3m in 2024.
metadata.content: Gianni Infantino: FIFA president received undeclared second salary payment of £1.3m from World Cup company | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Gianni Infantino: FIFA president received undeclared second salary payment of £1.3m from World Cup company FIFA president Gianni Infantino has been under pressure to resign after trying to sell stakes in FIFA tournaments to private investors; he has confirmed he will stand for re-election in March 2027 as planned; financial documents reveal Infantino received undisclosed payments Kaveh Solhekol Chief Correspondent Tuesday 13 October 2026 13:03, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol explains how FIFA president Gianni Infantino is under increasing pressure to resign. FIFA president Gianni Infantino is under increasing pressure to resign after it was revealed that he received an undeclared second salary of £1.3m in 2024. FIFA has committed to publishing Infantino's salary, bonus and allowances in its annual report every year since 2016. For 2024, he reported £3.88m ($5.1m) in salary but US tax filings show he also received £1.3m ($1.76m) from FWC2026, the company set up to organise and run this summer's World Cup, which was not publicly disclosed by FIFA in the annual report. messages.text: Jaissle sorry for Coventry loss as Carra says Newcastle 'beaten up' again

metadata.summary: Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle has apologised to the travelling fans following their 4-1 loss at Coventry, as Jamie Carragher said they were "beaten up" once again on the road.
metadata.content: Matthias Jaissle: Newcastle boss apologises for Coventry loss as Jamie Carragher says they were 'beaten up' | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Matthias Jaissle: Newcastle boss apologises for Coventry loss as Jamie Carragher says they were 'beaten up' Newcastle suffer second consecutive 4-1 away loss after defeat at Coventry; Toon boss Matthias Jaissle: "We can only apologise to the fans who came here"; Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher: "In their last two away games, they've been beaten up twice - and that's got to stop very quickly" Tuesday 13 October 2026 12:56, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Matthias Jaissle apologises to the travelling Newcastle fans for the 4-1 defeat to Coventry Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle has apologised to the travelling fans following their 4-1 loss at Coventry, as Jamie Carragher said they were "beaten up" once again on the road. The Magpies' previous away game a month ago also saw them defeated 4-1 on the Monday Night Football at Leeds. A second loss in three games comes after Jaissle had enjoyed an unbeaten five-game start across all competitions, but recent results have seen his side fall to 11th in the Premier League table. A wasteful Newcastle lost at Coventry despite having 19 shots, three big chances and more than double the number of touches in the opposition box than the home side.
